pure-announcement.rationale: An O'Reilly Radar essay proposing a named engineering pattern, with no product, release, or funding being announced.

duplicate.rationale: The existing context-layer concept covers assembling context for agents, but this note's core - pairing natural-language boundary artifacts with deterministic AST/CI enforcement and a strict precedence hierarchy - is not covered by it or any other neighbour.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The pattern is specified mechanically (artifact layout, Semgrep rules, CI stages) with an open-source reference implementation a reader can run.

durability.rationale: The core claim - govern generation with declared invariants enforced by deterministic build-time checks rather than probabilistic review - is an architectural trade-off independent of any model version or vendor.

actionability.rationale: It gives an implementable pipeline today: a /context directory layout, hybrid Markdown-plus-Semgrep artifacts, a precedence order for conflicts, and paired adversarial/acceptance CI gates.

atomicity.rationale: Beyond the central Context Compilation Pattern it bundles at least two separable ideas - tailor-made agent-legible architecture over opaque abstraction, and the data/instruction boundary softening inside context windows - each of which stands on its own.
